sample_unit: pill images (26,880 training images; test sample size not reported)
models_evaluated: Microsoft Azure Custom Vision (code-free deep learning) pill recognition model
TensorFlow Lite export (Windows PC and Android)

links.outcome: Pill recognition performance across deployment platforms and devices (online API, Windows PC, Android)
links.effect: Internal online API: 93.7% precision, 87.35% mAP. Offline Windows PC: 91.16% precision, 82.55% mAP. Offline Android app: 86.50% precision, 69.24% mAP.
links.quote: Performance of the model running offline on the Android application was further reduced to 86.50 % precision, 75.00 % recall, 77.83 % F1-score and 69.24 % mAP.

links.outcome: Performance in external real-world clinical testing versus internal testing
links.effect: External clinical testing via online API gave 83.10% precision, 71.39% recall, 75.76% F1, compared with 93.7% precision and 88.96% recall in internal testing.
links.quote: During external clinical testing through the online API an overall precision of 83.10 %, recall of 71.39 %, and F1-score of 75.76 % was achieved.

unlisted_practices: Using code-free deep learning platforms to develop clinical imaging models
Tailoring pill recognition models to a regional formulary or specific clinic's medications

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates a code-free deep learning pill recognition model using clinical pharmacist-captured images across several platforms (cloud API vs. edge devices), but evaluates pure technical accuracy across platforms rather than testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
